title: LEN gives declared length; LEN_TRIM gives logical content length — using the wrong one mishandles blank-padding
sourceContent:
SUBROUTINE EMIT_RECORD(NAME, RECLEN)
C     LEN(NAME) returns the DECLARED length (CHARACTER*32 -> 32),
C     regardless of content. LEN_TRIM(NAME) returns the position of
C     the last non-blank character (i.e. content length). Confusing
C     the two writes either a too-short record (NAME truncated) or
C     a too-long one (blank-padded out to 32 every time).
      IMPLICIT NONE
      CHARACTER*32 NAME
      INTEGER      RECLEN
C     Engineer meant LEN_TRIM here:
      RECLEN = LEN(NAME)
      END
notes: Engineers confuse LEN and LEN_TRIM constantly. The bug is invisible on inputs that happen to fill the entire CHARACTER*N width and breaks on shorter inputs. The spec must flag the intent + recommend the SME confirm which length the caller actually wants.
